clue.text: French journalist with courtesy title's feat of endurance

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat, the revolutionary journalist murdered in his bath
Hon, short for Honourable, is a British courtesy title

explanation.surface: A French reporter with an honorific pulls off some remarkable act of stamina.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance race of 26 miles is the classic test of stamina, and the word extends to any gruelling, lengthy effort.

clue.text: Doctor goes round country for some wool

indicators.note: goes round means the doctor encloses the country

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A physician travels around a nation to buy wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is a fine soft wool from the Merino breed of sheep.

clue.text: Stands topless and bolts

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word for stands is removed

parts.note: trivets are three-legged stands for pots

explanation.surface: Someone stands without a top on and then runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolts' suggests fleeing, but it is the noun for metal fasteners.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivets are metal pins used to fasten plates together, much like bolts.

clue.text: Fixture that might prove gripping for Windsor?

definitions.text: Fixture that might prove gripping for Windsor?

parts.words: Fixture that might prove gripping for Windsor?
parts.note: a Windsor is a style of necktie knot, and this clasp holds a tie in place against the shirt

explanation.surface: Some fitting that the royal Windsors would find riveting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windsor' suggests the royal family, but it is the Windsor knot in a necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: This clasp fixes a necktie, perhaps knotted Windsor-style, to the shirt front by gripping it.

clue.text: Past one's peak in more ways than one

definitions.text: Past one's peak in more ways than one

parts.words: Past one's peak in more ways than one
parts.note: the idiom for being too old, and literally having gone beyond the top of a rise

explanation.surface: Someone is past their best in several senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means past one's prime, and literally describes being beyond a summit.

clue.text: American with old Bob grieves audibly in trial

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated S

indicators.note: audibly says the letters entered are a word that sounds like the synonym of grieves

parts.note: someone grieving sighs

explanation.surface: An American and an elderly man named Bob sob loudly in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' is not a name here but slang for the pre-decimal British shilling, written S.
explanation.definitionFit: The assizes were periodic English county court sessions where criminal cases were heard, hence a trial.

clue.text: Work hastily about first half of July to make ramp

indicators.note: about means the word for work hastily surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to skimp is to do a job carelessly and quickly

indicators.note: first half of takes the opening two letters of the month name

explanation.surface: Rushed work in early July produces a ramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski jump is the steep ramp skiers launch from to fly through the air.

clue.text: How bright idea may come to one

definitions.text: How bright idea may come to one

parts.words: How bright idea may come to one
parts.note: a brainwave arrives suddenly, and a bright idea is pictured as a burst of light

explanation.surface: A description of the way inspiration strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly, and a 'bright' idea fits the image of a burst of light.

clue.text: Still having fancy diet before bed?

parts.note: still as in 'even more', for example 'still better' or 'even better'

indicators.note: fancy says the letters of diet are dressed up in another order

explanation.surface: Someone is still on an elaborate diet ahead of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the time before going to bed.

clue.text: Critic regularly irked 'Spectator'

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word irked, here the second and fourth

parts.note: a spectator is one who watches, a viewer

explanation.surface: A critic was repeatedly annoyed by The Spectator magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Spectator' look like the magazine's title; it is just an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic who writes assessments of books, plays or films is a reviewer by profession.

clue.text: End with almost everything stopping dry

indicators.note: stopping as in plugging a gap: the shortened word sits inside the other

parts.note: fine weather is dry weather

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for everything is dropped

parts.note: everything is all

explanation.surface: Something finishes when nearly everything stops being dry.
explanation.definitionFit: The finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music, its conclusion.

clue.text: Isn't allowed to include electronic sheet of paper

indicators.note: to include means the two words are split to hold the single letter

parts.note: is not allowed means is not let
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Someone is forbidden to put electronic material on a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet of decorated writing paper for short letters.

clue.text: Pair having time to produce rhyme

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Two people take time to write some verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is two successive rhyming lines of verse, so loosely a rhyme.

clue.text: Pitched battle that's first-class perhaps

parts.note: a contest fought on a pitch between English shires, which in cricket has first-class status

explanation.surface: A fierce set battle of the highest quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitched battle' suggests warfare; here it is a game on a pitch. English county cricket games are 'first-class' matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A game between two English county sides, in cricket rated first-class, is a battle on a pitch.

clue.text: Before alleged, that's taken for granted

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
something alleged is supposed

explanation.surface: What was claimed earlier is now simply assumed.
explanation.definitionFit: To presuppose is to assume in advance, so something presupposed is taken for granted.

clue.text: Blue is smoother, without question

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the smoothing tool goes around the question

parts.note: a sander is a tool for smoothing surfaces

explanation.surface: A sad person is calmer and has no doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like the colour or sadness; it is the slang verb meaning to spend recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue money is British slang for wasting it, the same as to squander it.

clue.text: Thrilled lout was in contention outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for competed goes around the word for lout

parts.note: vied means competed, was in contention
a brat is an ill-mannered youngster, a lout

explanation.surface: A yob was excited to be in the running, though left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilled can mean quivered or throbbed, physically shaking, which is to vibrate.

clue.text: Nimble comedian Edward having an alert mind

parts.note: nimble means quick
a wit is a clever, funny person
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: An agile comic called Edward is sharp-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick-witted describes someone who thinks fast and responds sharply, with a nimble, alert mind.

clue.text: Bird finding trees bending in Malaysian city

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the city's initials

parts.note: KL is the common short form of Kuala Lumpur

indicators.note: bending says the letters of trees are twisted into another shape

explanation.surface: A bird spots trees swaying in a city in Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon that hovers before swooping on prey, a bird of prey.

clue.text: Waste time in prison

parts.note: dung is animal waste
an eon is an immeasurably long time

explanation.surface: Someone wastes their time while locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell for holding prisoners, a castle's prison.

clue.text: Second best part that's a laugh

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: The second-best role in a show is a comic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a very funny person or thing is called a scream, a real laugh.

clue.text: Quite a bit of restraint or tension

indicators.note: quite a bit of means most but not all of the word restraint supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A great deal of self-control or nervous stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain is stress or tension, as in the strain on a rope or on nerves.

clue.text: Chocolate therefore left in pressurised container

parts.note: Aero is a British bubbly chocolate bar
so means therefore

explanation.surface: Chocolate has been left inside a pressurised can.
explanation.walkthrough: AERO is a well-known British chocolate bar full of air bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a can holding liquid under pressure, released as a fine spray.

clue.text: Feline coming to an unexpectedly abrupt end

definitions.text: Feline coming to an unexpectedly abrupt end

parts.words: Feline coming to an unexpectedly abrupt end
parts.note: a breed of cat from the Isle of Man that has no tail, so its body stops short where a tail is expected

explanation.surface: A cat meets a sudden, surprising death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cat's demise; the 'end' is its rear, which stops short with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed from the Isle of Man is known for being tailless, its back ending abruptly.

clue.text: Cheat thanks Romeo with daughter who's a feeble-minded person

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
ta is British informal for thanks
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A swindler thanks Romeo and his daughter, who is rather dim.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotard is someone weak-minded through old age, a senile person.

clue.text: React strangely over new tee and other things

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of react and tee are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone reacts oddly to a fresh golf tee and other items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges REACT together with TEE; 'over new' and 'and' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, usually shortened to etc., means 'and the rest', that is other things of the same kind.

clue.text: Puzzle as theologian's overcome by anger

indicators.note: overcome by means the theologian is enveloped by the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A puzzle in which a religious scholar is overwhelmed with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question or enigma, posed to be solved.

clue.text: Delivery of porcelain figure?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a left-arm wrist-spinner's ball that turns into a right-handed batsman
read as two words, a man made of china, a porcelain ornament

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's 'chinaman' is a left-arm unorthodox spin delivery; 'Delivery' looks like the arrival of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a specific cricket bowling type and, split in two, a figurine made of fine ceramic.
